content: Ganciclovir is indicated for the treatment of cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in immunocompromised adults, including those with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). The induction dose is 5 mg/kg administered intravenously every 12 hours, infused over one hour, for a duration of 14 to 21 days. Ganciclovir is also indicated for the prevention of CMV disease in adult transplant recipients at risk for CMV disease. The induction dose for this indication is 5 mg/kg intravenously once daily, infused over one hour, for 7 to 14 days. For primary or recurrent CMV infections, oral dosing of 1000 mg three times daily is recommended. For recurrent infections, intravenous dosing of 5-6 mg/kg 5-7 times per week may be used. Initial treatment should begin with ganciclovir at 5 mg/kg per dose intravenously every 12 hours. Once the therapy is tolerated, it can be transitioned to valganciclovir at 900 mg orally every 12 hours for 21-42 days or until clinical signs and symptoms resolve. For recurrent CMV infections, a maintenance dose of 5 mg/kg intravenously once daily may be used. Drug Interactions: 1. Ganciclovir and Abacavir: Co-administration increases the risk of hematologic toxicity. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. 2. Ganciclovir and Bacitracin: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent use or use alternative drugs. 3. Ganciclovir and Imipenem/Cilastatin: Co-administration may increase the risk of seizures. Avoid unless the potential benefit outweighs the risk. 4. Ganciclovir and Ropinterferon Alfa-2b: Co-administration may lead to additive myelosuppression. Avoid use or monitor closely for excessive myelosuppression. 5. Ganciclovir and Talimogene Laherparepvec: Ganciclovir decreases the effects of talimogene laherparepvec due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Ganciclovir and Zidovudine: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Ganciclovir and Hydroxyurea: Combination may increase the risk of myelosuppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Ganciclovir and Ifosfamide: Co-administration may enhance the toxicities of myelosuppressive agents. Monitor for increased risk of myelosuppression. 9. Ganciclovir and Lamivudine: Co-administration increases the risk of hematologic toxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 10. Ganciclovir and Mycophenolate: Ganciclovir increases the level or effect of mycophenolate by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 11. Ganciclovir and Peramivir: Ganciclovir increases peramivir levels by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor for nephrotoxicity. 12. Ganciclovir and Pretomanid: Pretomanid inhibits OAT3, potentially increasing ganciclovir levels. Monitor for adverse effects and consider dosage reduction. 13. Ganciclovir and Probenecid: Ganciclovir increases probenecid levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 14. Ganciclovir and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration may increase serum concentrations of tenofovir. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ganciclovir and Ublituximab: Ublituximab decreases the effects of ganciclovir due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor. 16. Ganciclovir and Vadadustat: Vadadustat may increase exposure to OAT3 substrates, including ganciclovir. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust dosage as needed. 17. Ganciclovir and Voclosporin: Co-administration may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 18. Ganciclovir and NSAIDs (e.g., Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Ketorolac): NSAIDs may increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, but caution is advised. 19. Ganciclovir and Sulfamethoxazole: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 20. Ganciclovir and Flucytosine: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Ganciclovir and Pentamidine: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Ganciclovir and Dapsone: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Ganciclovir and Entecavir: Co-administration may increase serum concentrations of both drugs by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Ganciclovir and Mesalamine: Mesalamine may increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 25. Ganciclovir and Bendroflumethiazide: Co-administration may increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Ganciclovir and Cephalosporins (e.g., Cefadroxil, Cefamandole): Cephalosporins may increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 27. Ganciclovir and Diclofenac: Diclofenac may increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 28. Ganciclovir and Nabumetone: Nabumetone may increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Ganciclovir and Piroxicam: Piroxicam may increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Ganciclovir and Salsalate: Salsalate may increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 31. Ganciclovir and Sulfasalazine: Sulfasalazine may increase ganciclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown.
